item.title: After Bumble announced that the famously women-forward app would...
item.description: After Bumble announced that the famously women-forward app would be walking back on its trademark policy and allowing men to make the first move, it would seem like the ball is once again back in the male court. But it isn't quite so simple. As Senior Editor @magdajtaylor asks in her Fair Play column, the shift may be yet another sign of the continued dating app fatigue that is plaguing singles regardless of gender. At the link in bio, she explores whether anyone these days is up to the task of initiating romance.Executive Producer, Video: @hi_im_danEditor, Video: 3DJ PicturesProduction Services: @wynck.co

item.title: On August 5th, 6, we lost one of our nation's most universally b...
item.description: On August 5th, 6, we lost one of our nation's most universally beloved figures: Dolly Parton. She will always be remembered for her endless generosity, her country pluck and—we say this with complete respect and admiration—for her over-the-top breasts.Sex and sexuality, in Dolly's world, are natural—even if her boobs weren't. It's only right, then, Senior Editor @magdajtaylor argues, that we celebrate her life by embracing the same style of gaudiness and reverence for the bosom she was known for. Is posting pictures of your cleavage in her name a little bit tacky? Of course. So was Dolly.Tits out for Dolly. Link in bio.

item.title: I was featured in @washingtonpost this weekend for my work on th...
item.description: I was featured in @washingtonpost this weekend for my work on the state of heterosexuality and the gender war. @shadihamid and I discussed how digital narratives have fractured our relationship with desire and the possibilities we still have to repair it. Thank you to Shadi for the thoughtful interview and to @jelani.rice for the photos of me in my home.

item.description: ‼️Is it “Okay” to Like Men? (W/ Magdalene J. Taylor)‼️Senior editor at Playboy, Magdalene J. Taylor, returns to Bad Faith to discuss her viral (and somewhat infamous) New York Times essay, “There’s Nothing Wrong With Wanting Men.” Responding to a trend toward “hetero-pessimism,” or a cynical feeling that heterosexual relationships are beyond repair due largely to something ‘wrong’ with men, she offers a counter argument: There’s never been a better time to be straight. Reasonable minds can disagree.
